title: Liber Esther
authorsDisplay: Anselm of Laon and his school

fontes.raw: Vide inter opera B. Hieronymi, tom. VIII.
RAB., expos. in lib. Esther, tom. III.

heads.la: B. HIERONYMI IN LIBRUM ESTHER PROLOGUS.
heads.en: THE PROLOGUE OF BLESSED JEROME ON THE BOOK OF ESTHER.

headnotes.la: …n factura vituli. Nec Salomon in sorde libidinis. Sic Assuerus in isto judicio, ut in liberali convivio Christum significat, sicut Isaias in Cyro rege Persarum Christum signat, de quo postea subjungit
headnotes.en: …mon in the filth of lust. So Assuerus in that judgment, as in the bountiful banquet, signifies Christ, just as Isaias in Cyrus the king of the Persians signifies Christ, of whom he afterwards subjoins

headnotes.la: Magnatum vel primitivorum fidelium primi refecti sunt, secundum illud
headnotes.en: The first of the great ones, or of the primitive faithful, were refreshed, according to that

headnotes.la: Id est, doctoribus de quibus dicitur
headnotes.en: That is, by the teachers, of whom it is said

headnotes.la: Smaragdus a nimia viriditate sui sic vocatur. Parium, genus marmoris candidissimum. Per virorem enim fidei et candorem castitatis construitur fundamentum humilitatis
headnotes.en: The emerald is so called from its exceeding greenness. Parian, a kind of most white marble. For by the greenness of faith and the whiteness of chastity is built the foundation of humility

headnotes.la: Et: « Qui se humiliat exaltabitur [n: (Luc. X)]. Et alibi
headnotes.en: And: « He that humbleth himself shall be exalted [n: (Luc. X)]. And elsewhere

headnotes.la: etc. Nemo cogitur spirituale donum accipere: filios vult Deus, non servos: voluntatem vult, non necessitatem, secundum illud
headnotes.en: etc. No one is compelled to receive a spiritual gift: God wills sons, not slaves: he wills the will, not necessity, according to that

headnotes.la: etc. Hic novissimus in ordine septem sapientum numeratus, sententiam promulgat, et Paulum apostolum significat qui dicit
headnotes.en: etc. He, reckoned last in the order of the seven wise men, promulgates the sentence, and signifies Paul the apostle, who says

headnotes.la: Et contradicentibus Judaeis et zelo repletis ait
headnotes.en: And to the Jews contradicting and filled with zeal he says

headnotes.la: Id est, fideles animas Spiritu sancti gratia regeneratas atque dedicatas quae ejus sequuntur vestigia, fide, doctrina, et operatione, de quibus dicitur
headnotes.en: That is, faithful souls regenerated and dedicated by the grace of the Holy Spirit, which follow her [the Church's] footsteps in faith, in doctrine, and in work, of whom it is said

headnotes.la: Non sufficit Christo primitivam sibi sociare Ecclesiam, sed per praedicatores de gentibus multitudinem acquisivit copiosam; unde
headnotes.en: It did not suffice Christ to associate to himself the primitive Church, but through preachers he acquired a plentiful multitude from among the Gentiles; whence

headnotes.la: etc. Duobus Testamentis, in quibus scriptum est, quae justis praemia, quae injustis debeantur supplicia; unde
headnotes.en: etc. By the two Testaments, in which it is written what rewards are due to the just, what punishments to the unjust; whence

headnotes.la: …entiam quam soli Deo debuerunt, in sese transferre contendunt. Eos autem qui consentire nolunt, odiis et cruciatibus persequuntur: sed justo Dei judicio in insidiis suis capiuntur iniqui. Unde dicitur
headnotes.en: … which they owed to God alone. But those who will not consent they persecute with hatreds and with torments: but by the just judgment of God the wicked are taken in their own snares. Whence it is said

headnotes.la: …runt, et Dominum prophetarum et apostolos, ejus generis nobilitatem propter incredulitatem et duritiam cordis perdentes, qui per Isaiam principes Sodomorum et populus Gomorrhae dicuntur. Unde Ezechiel
headnotes.en: …e Lord of the prophets, and the apostles, losing the nobility of their race because of unbelief and hardness of heart, who by Isaias are called princes of Sodom and people of Gomorrha. Whence Ezechiel

headnotes.la: Sic magister Ecclesiae intercessione reginae, de qua dicitur
headnotes.en: So the master of the Church, by the intercession of the queen, of whom it is said

headnotes.la: …ntroitum, ut post laetabundus supernum intret palatium. Si quis quaerat quomodo rex justissimus tormenta inferat innocentibus, sciat hoc non esse ex voto malitiae, sed ex summi consilii nutu procedere
headnotes.en: … into the palace on high. If any man ask how a most just king inflicts torments upon the innocent, let him know that this is not from a wish of malice, but proceeds from the nod of the highest counsel
[var: Vulg. Wisd. 7:30 *sapientiam autem non vincit malitia*, "but malice doth not overcome wisdom" — subject and object are reversed in what Migne prints, which also has no negative]

headnotes.la: Regiminis potentiam vel passionis crucem, per quam acquisivit potestatem, de qua dicitur
headnotes.en: The power of governance, or the cross of the passion, through which he acquired the power of which it is said

headnotes.la: Dilatio petendi non deputatur segnitiei, sed patientiae. Non enim in praesenti sed in futuro bonis et malis retribuetur merces: cras enim pro futuro ponitur, unde
headnotes.en: … delay in asking is not reckoned to sloth, but to patience. For not in the present but in the future shall the wage be repaid to the good and to the wicked: for to morrow is put for the future, whence
[var: Vulg. Gen. 30:33 *respondebitque mihi cras justitia mea*, "shall answer for me"] And of the lamb it is said

headnotes.la: etc. In se mobilis permanens cursus temporum et actus omnium contemplatur, et nulla eum latet cogitatio cui omnia praesentia; unde Apostolus
headnotes.en: …obilis*; read *immobilis*, "unmoved"] in himself, he [God] contemplates the course of times and the acts of all men, and no thought lies hid from him to whom all things are present; whence the Apostle

headnotes.la: …ustrati honorantur diademate regiae dignitatis, tanquam membra summi regis. Ascendunt super equum regium, id est, super populum fidelium in quorum cordibus residet rex angelorum; unde Habacuc propheta
headnotes.en: …iadem of royal dignity, as members of the highest king. They mount upon the royal horse, that is, upon the people of the faithful in whose hearts the king of angels resides; whence Habacuc the prophet

headnotes.la: Haec mutatio dexterae Excelsi, qui si videbatur gloriosior, infra alios apparet vilior et inferior, secundum illud
headnotes.en: This is the change of the right hand of the Most High, he who, if he seemed the more glorious, appears beneath others baser and lower, according to that

headnotes.la: … Synagogae compressa est superbia, Ecclesiae humilitas exaltata. Sic persecutores fidei ad nihilum sunt redacti: confessores Christi in toto orbe exaltati. Caput in caudam, et cauda in caput versa est
headnotes.en: …ility of the Church exalted. So were the persecutors of the faith brought to nothing: the confessors of Christ exalted in the whole world. The head was turned into the tail, and the tail into the head

headnotes.la: …m electos ad delicias paradisi invitante, reginam pro salute sua deprecari contendit, sed tempus opportunum non habuit. Sero enim quaeruntur salutis remedia, cum mortis imminent pericula; unde Salomon
headnotes.en: … paradise, he [Aman] strove to beseech the queen for his own safety, but had not a fitting time. For too late are the remedies of salvation sought, when the perils of death are at hand; whence Solomon

headnotes.la: Doctores legis significat, qui scelera et dolos Judaeorum praedixerunt, unde Moyses
headnotes.en: It signifies the doctors of the law, who foretold the crimes and the deceits of the Jews, whence Moses
[var: Vulg. Deut. 31:29 *declinabitis cito de via quam praecepi vobis*, "will quickly decline from the way which I have commanded you"] And in the Gospel

headnotes.la: Tenet Esther domum Aman, hostis Judaeorum, cum Ecclesia possidet mundum, quem possederat diabolus, hostis Christianorum; unde
headnotes.en: Esther holds the house of Aman, the enemy of the Jews, when the Church possesses the world, which the devil, the enemy of Christians, had possessed; whence

headnotes.la: Dignitatem et honorem quem Judaei scientia legis, et prophetarum, et cultu religionis habuerunt; unde in Proverbiis
headnotes.en: The dignity and the honour which the Jews had by the knowledge of the law and of the prophets, and by the practice of religion; whence in the Proverbs

headnotes.la: Laudante et praedicante instantiam magistrorum, a Domino pro gratia gratiam accipiunt in conspectu conditoris omnium; unde
headnotes.en: [The king] praising and proclaiming the earnestness of the masters, they receive from the Lord grace for grace in the sight of the creator of all; whence

headnotes.la: etc. In superbia mundi debellanda. Nam Susis equitatio vel evertens interpretatur; unde Salvator ait
headnotes.en: etc. In the pride of the world that is to be overcome. For Susis is interpreted riding, or overturning; whence the Saviour says

headnotes.la: Quia doctorum actio laudabilis, et potentia virtutum, honorem et reverentiam tribuit multitudini fidelium. Unde in Actibus apostolorum
headnotes.en: Because the praiseworthy action of the teachers, and the power of their virtues, bestows honour and reverence upon the multitude of the faithful. Whence in the Acts of the Apostles

headnotes.la: unde legitur alibi: « Fiebat enim omni animae timor [n: (Ibid. II)]. Item
headnotes.en: whence it is read elsewhere: « For fear came upon every soul [n: (Ibid. II)]. Likewise

headnotes.la: … sabbatum aeternae quietis habent: alii, usque ad ultimum resurrectionis diem in carne perdurantes superatis hostibus universis subito immutati, quietem animarum et corporum percipiunt; unde Apostolus
headnotes.en: …h of eternal rest: others, enduring in the flesh until the last day of the resurrection, all their enemies being overcome, suddenly changed, receive the rest of souls and of bodies; whence the Apostle

headnotes.la: etc. Sors in urnam missa, dispositionem cujuslibet rei in hominis mente significat, cujus eventum non humanum, sed divinum regit arbitrium, unde Salomon
headnotes.en: etc. The lot cast into the urn signifies the disposing of any matter whatsoever in the mind of man, the outcome of which not human but divine judgment governs, whence Solomon
